EC2NewGen.^description: Instance Type Currency: {$COUNT} of your instances are running in an older generation of instance type. Upgrade to the latest generation of instance type to gain better perfomance and lower cost.

EC2DetailedMonitor.^description: Detailed Monitoring: Detailed Monitoring has not been enabled for {$COUNT} of your instances. Enable Detailed Monitoring to get monitoring metrics with higher frequency.

EC2IamProfile.^description: IAM Instance Profile: {$COUNT} of your instances lack an IAM profile association. Associate IAM profile to control AWS API request securely.

EC2EIPNotInUse.^description: Elastic IP Not In Use: {$COUNT} of your Elastic IP is not associated to any instance. Release unused Elastic IP to save cost.

EC2KeyPairNotInUse.^description: Unused Key Pairs: {$COUNT} of your EC2 key pairs are not associated with any running instance. Remove unused key pairs to reduce the attack surface and improve security hygiene.

EC2IMDSv2.^description: IMDSv2 Not Enforced: {$COUNT} of your instances have not enforced IMDSv2 (Instance Metadata Service v2). IMDSv2 adds session-based authentication and mitigates SSRF attacks. Set HttpTokens to 'required' to enforce IMDSv2.

EC2StoppedTooLong.^description: Stopped Instances (>30 days): {$COUNT} of your instances have been in a stopped state for more than 30 days. Stopped instances still incur EBS storage costs. Consider creating an AMI and terminating the instance, or terminate if no longer needed.

EC2NoTerminationProtection.^description: No Termination Protection: {$COUNT} of your instances do not have termination protection enabled. Enable termination protection to prevent accidental deletion of critical instances.

EC2SSMNotManaged.^description: SSM Not Managed: {$COUNT} of your instances are not managed by AWS Systems Manager. SSM provides patching, compliance visibility, remote access, and inventory management. Install the SSM agent and attach the required IAM role.

EC2MemoryMonitor.^description: EC2 Memory Monitoring: Memory monitoring has not been enabled for {$COUNT} of your instances. Install CloudWatch agent and enable the monitoring

EC2DiskMonitor.^description: EC2 Disk Monitoring: Disk monitoring has not been enabled for {$COUNT} of your instances. Install CloudWatch agent and enable the monitoring

EC2Active.^description: EC2 Active: {$COUNT} of your instances have not been running for more than 7 days. Terminate intances that are not required.

EC2SGNumber.^description: EC2 Security Group Association: {$COUNT} of your instances have more than 50 security groups associated. Please reduce the number of security groups.

EC2LowUtilization.^description: EC2 Low Utilization: {$COUNT} of your instances have low utilization. Decrease instance size to save cost.

EC2HighUtilization.^description: EC2 High Utilization: {$COUNT} of your instances have high utilization. Increase instance size to improve performance.

EC2SpikyUtilization.^description: EC2 Spiky Utilization: {$COUNT} of your instances have spiky utilization. Switch to burstable instance to save cost.

EC2InstancePublicIP.^description: EC2 with Public IP: {$COUNT} of your instances associated public IP. Disable unused public IP from instances.

EC2InstanceAutoPublicIP.^description: EC2 with Auto Assign IP: {$COUNT} of your instances enabled auto-assign public IP. Disable unused public IP from instances.

EC2SubnetAutoPublicIP.^description: EC2 Subnet with Auto Assign IP: {$COUNT} of your instances has enabled auto-assign public IP in subnet configuration.
EC2SubnetAutoPublicIP.shortDesc: EC2 Subnet with Auto Assign IP

EC2HasTag.^description: EC2 without tagging: {$COUNT} of your instances has no tagging. Tag your EC2 instances.

EC2AMD.^description: EC2 instance family with AMD chips: {$COUNT} of your instances can change to intance type powered by AMD chips

EC2Graviton.^description: EC2 instance family with Graviton chips: {$COUNT} of your instances can change to instance type powered by Graviton chips.

EBSStoppedInstance.^description: Storage Utilization: {$COUNT} of EBS storage volumes are attached to stopped instances. Remove volumes to reduce the storage cost.
EBSStoppedInstance.shortDesc: Remove EBS attached to Stopped EC2
ref: [Delete EBS Volume that you no longer need]<https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-deleting-volume.html>

EBSEncrypted.^description: Storage Encyrption: {$COUNT} of EBS storage volumes are not encrypted. Enable encryption for EBS volumes to meet security and compliance requirements.

EBSNewGen.^description: Storage Type Currency: {$COUNT} of EBS volumes are on an older storage type. Upgrade to latest generation of storage type to gain better performance and lower cost

EBSInUse.^description: Storage Utilization: {$COUNT} of EBS storage volumes are not attached to any instances. Remove unused volumes to reduce the storage cost.
ref: [Controlling AWS costs by deleting unused Amazon EBS volumes]<https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/mt/controlling-your-aws-costs-by-deleting-unused-amazon-ebs-volumes/>

EBSSnapshot.^description: Storage Snapshot: {$COUNT} of EBS has no snapshot(s) available. Enable regular backups to prevent data loss.

EBSUpToDateSnapshot.^description: Storage Snapshot Up To Date: {$COUNT} of EBS has outdated snapshots. Take a new snapshot.

EBSSnapshotIsPublic.^description: Public Snapshot: {$COUNT} of EBS snapshots is available to public. Modify snapshot permission to private.
EBSSnapshotIsPublic.remediation: aws ec2 modify-snapshot-attribute --snapshot-id {ResourceId} --attribute createVolumePermission --operation-type remove --group-names all

EBSSnapshotDeletedVolume.^description: Snapshot from Deleted Volume: You have EBS snapshots retained from deleted volumes. Use Data Lifecycle Manager to manage them.
EBSSnapshotDeletedVolume.shortDesc: Use Data Lifecycle Manager to manage snapshot

EBSLowUtilization.^description: EBS Low Utilization: {$COUNT} of EBS volume has less than 1 IOPS utilization for past 7 days. Remove volumes that are not required to reduce costs.
ref: [Controlling AWS costs by deleting unused Amazon EBS volumes]<https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/mt/controlling-your-aws-costs-by-deleting-unused-amazon-ebs-volumes/>

EBSHighUtilization.^description: EBS High Utilization: {$COUNT} of EBS volume have high IOPS utilization for past 7 days. Increase provisioned IOPS to improve performance.

EBSRightSizing.^description: EBS Right Sizing: {$COUNT} of EBS volume has low IOPS utilization for past 7 days. Reduce provisioned IOPS to reduce costs.

EBSFastSnapshot.^description: EBS Fast Snapshot Enabled: {$COUNT} of EBS volumes has Fast Snapshot Restores enabled. Only enable Fast Snapshot Restore if necessary as it will generate additional cost.

SGDefaultInUsed.^description: Default Security Group: {$COUNT} of default security groups are utilized. It is recommended to create custom security group that configured with specific rules.

SGSensitivePortOpenToAll.^description: Sensitive ports open to all: {$COUNT} of security group have sensitive ports (DNS, MongoDB, MSSQL, MySQL, NFS, OracleDB PostgreSQL, RDP, SMTP, SMTPS, SSH) open to all IPs. Recommend to open only for required IP.

SGAllTCPOpen.^description: All TCP Ports Open: {$COUNT} security groups has all TCP ports open. It is recommended to open only specific ports that are required.

SGAllUDPOpen.^description: All UDP Ports Open: {$COUNT} security groups has all UDP ports open. It is recommended to open only specific ports that are required.

SGAllPortOpen.^description: All Ports Open: {$COUNT} of security group has all ports open. It is recommended to open only specific ports that are required.

SGAllPortOpenToAll.^description: All Ports Open to All: {$COUNT} of security group has all port open to all IP. It is recommended to open only specific ports to specific IPs that are required.

SGEncryptionInTransit.^description: Encryption In Transit: {$COUNT} of security group has ports enabled without encryption in transit. It is recommended to use ports with encryption in transit

SGRuleNumber.^description: High Number of Rules: {$COUNT} of security group have more than 50 rules. Restructure and reuse the rules.

SGDefaultDisallowTraffic.^description: Default Security Group with Rules: {$COUNT} of default security group have rules. Remove rules in default security group

ComputeOptimizerEnabled.^description: Compute Optimizer Not Enabled: Compute Optimizer of your account is not enabled. Enable Compute Optimizer to get resources recommendations.

CEReservedInstance.^description: Reserved Instance Recommendation: Reserved Instances recommendations available in Cost Explorer

CESavingsPlans.^description: Savings Plans Recommendation: Savings Plans recommendations available in Cost Explorer

ELBListenerInsecure.^description: Insecure Listener: {$COUNT} of ELB listeners are using insecure protocols. Please use secure protocols.

ELBSGNumber.^description: ELB Security Group Association: {$COUNT} of your ELBs have more than 50 security groups associated. Please reduce the number of security groups

ELBCrossZone.^description: ELB Cross Zone Load Balancing: {$COUNT} of your ELBs do not have cross zone load balancing enabled. Enable cross zone load balancing to improve availability.

ELBConnectionDraining.^description: ELB Connection Draining: {$COUNT} of your ELBs have not enabled connection draining.

ELBClassicLB.^description: ELB Classic Load Balancer: {$COUNT} of your ELBs are Classic Load Balancers. Migrate to a newer generation of ELB.

ELBEnableWAF.^description: ALB Web Application Firewall: {$COUNT} of your ALBs have not enabled WAF.

ELBSGRulesMatch.^description: ALB Security Group Rules Configuration: {$COUNT} of Security Group in your ALBs has different port opened.

ASGELBHealthCheckValidation.^description: ELB Health Check Validation: {$COUNT} of your ASG have ELB health check enabled without ELB association.

ASGELBHealthCheckEnabled.^description: ELB Health Check Enabled: {$COUNT} of your ASG ELB association without ELB health check enabled

ASGInstancesRemoved.^description: Instance Removed: {$COUNT} of your ASG have no instances association.
ref: [Attached or Detached, Instances or LB to ASG]<https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-detach-attach-instances.html>

ASGTargetGroupELBExist.^description: Target Group without ELB: {$COUNT} of target group your ASG have no ELB association.
ref: [Attached or Detached, Instances or LB to ASG]<https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-detach-attach-instances.html>

ASGClassicLBExist.^description: Classic LB Deleted: {$COUNT} of your ASG are associated with a deleted Classic Load Balancer.

ASGAMIExist.^description: Launch Configuration/Template AMI Deleted: {$COUNT} of Launch Configuration/Template AMI of your ASG are using deleted AMI

ASGIMDSv2.^description: Launch Configuration/Template IMDSv2: {$COUNT} of Launch Configuration/Template have not enable IMDSv2

SQLServerEOL.^description:
You have {$COUNT} EC2 running on EOL SQL Server version. To modernize your SQL Server workloads, consider refactoring to AWS Cloud native databases like Amazon Aurora.
To move to a fully managed database, consider replatforming to Amazon Relational Database Service (Amazon RDS).
To upgrade your SQL Server on Amazon EC2, consider using the automation runbook to simplify your upgrade. For more information, see the AWS Systems Manager documentation.

If you can’t upgrade your SQL Server on Amazon EC2, consider the End-of-Support Migration Program (EMP) for Windows Server.Each SQL Server version offers 10 years of support, including 5 years of mainstream support and 5 years of extended support. After the end of support, the SQL Server version won’t receive regular security updates. Running applications with unsupported SQL Server versions can bring security or compliance risks.

VPCFlowLogEnabled.^description: You have {$COUNT} VPC has not enable VPC Flow Log. VPC Flow Log provide visibility into network traffic that traverses the VPC.

NACLAssociated.^description: You have {$COUNT} Network ACL has no subnet association. Remove unused Network ACL to improve operation efficiency.

NACLSensitivePort.^description: You have {$COUNT} Network ACL has unrestricted ingress access to SSH/RDP port. Remove ingress access for the sensitive port
NACLSensitivePort.shortDesc: Remove unrestricted ingress access to sensitive port

WindowsOSOutdated.^description: You have {$COUNT} EC2 running on EOL Windows Server version. You will no longer receive patches from Microsoft. Please upgrade your Windows to non-EOL edition

WindowsOSNotLatest.^description: You have {$COUNT} EC2 running on EOL Windows Server version. You will no longer receive patches from Microsoft. Please consider upgrade your Windows to non-EOL edition

EBSEncryptionByDefault.^description: EBS Encryption by Default: EBS encryption by default is not enabled in this region. Enable encryption by default to ensure all new EBS volumes are encrypted automatically.

EBSVolumeDataClassification.^description: EBS Volume Data Classification: {$COUNT} of your EBS volumes lack data classification tags. Tag volumes with data classification (e.g., 'DataClassification', 'Sensitivity') for compliance and governance.

EBSSnapshotFirstArchived.^description: EBS Snapshot First Archived: {$COUNT} of your first snapshots in snapshot chains are archived. Avoid archiving first snapshots as they significantly impact restore time.

EBSSnapshotComplianceArchive.^description: EBS Snapshot Compliance Archive: {$COUNT} of your old compliance snapshots are not archived. Archive old compliance snapshots to reduce storage costs while meeting retention requirements.

EC2EbsOptimized.^description: EBS-Optimized Instances: {$COUNT} of your instances support EBS optimization but do not have it enabled. Enable EBS optimization for better I/O performance.

EC2RootVolumeImplications.^description: Root Volume Implications: {$COUNT} of your instances have root volumes with DeleteOnTermination enabled but lack recent snapshots. Ensure root volumes have proper backup strategy.

EBSSnapshotLatestArchived.^description: EBS Snapshot Latest Archived: {$COUNT} of your volumes have their most recent snapshot archived. Keep the latest snapshot in standard tier for quick restore capability.
EBSSnapshotLatestArchived.shortDesc: Keep Latest Snapshot in Standard Tier

VPCMultiAZ.^description: VPC Multi-AZ: {$COUNT} of your VPCs have subnets in only one availability zone. Distribute subnets across multiple AZs for high availability.

ELBMultiAZ.^description: ELB Multi-AZ: {$COUNT} of your load balancers are configured with fewer than 2 availability zones. Enable multiple AZs for high availability.
ELBMultiAZ.shortDesc: Enable Multiple AZs for Load Balancers

ASGMultiAZ.^description: ASG Multi-AZ: {$COUNT} of your Auto Scaling Groups are configured with fewer than 2 availability zones. Distribute instances across multiple AZs for high availability.

ASGTargetTrackingPolicy.^description: ASG Target Tracking Policy: {$COUNT} of your Auto Scaling Groups do not use target tracking scaling policies. Use target tracking for better scaling behavior and cost optimization.

EC2ServiceQuotas.^description: EC2 Service Quotas: {$COUNT} of your EC2 resource quotas are approaching limits (>80% utilization). Monitor and request quota increases to prevent service disruptions.

ASGScalingCooldowns.^description: ASG Scaling Cooldowns: {$COUNT} of your Auto Scaling Groups have very short or no scaling cooldown period. Configure appropriate cooldown periods (300+ seconds recommended) to prevent scaling thrashing.

ComputeOptimizerEnhancedMetrics.^description: Compute Optimizer Enhanced Metrics: Enhanced infrastructure metrics are not enabled for Compute Optimizer. Enable enhanced metrics for better optimization recommendations with 93-day analysis period.

EC2SeparateOSDataVolumes.^description: Separate OS and Data Volumes: {$COUNT} of your instances have only a root volume without separate data volumes. Separate OS and data volumes for better data management and persistence.

EC2InstanceStoreUsage.^description: Instance Store Usage: {$COUNT} of your instances have instance store-capable instance types but may not be utilizing instance store volumes. Consider using instance store for temporary high-performance storage needs.

ComputeOptimizerRightsizingPrefs.^description: Compute Optimizer Rightsizing Preferences: Rightsizing recommendation preferences have not been customized. Customize preferences to get more accurate rightsizing recommendations for your workloads.

ComputeOptimizerExportRecommendations.^description: Compute Optimizer Export Recommendations: No recommendation export jobs are configured. Export recommendations to S3 for tracking and governance purposes.

ec2AmiPublic.^description: Public AMI: {$COUNT} AMI(s) owned by this account are shared publicly (launch permission group 'all'). Anyone can launch them and read their snapshots, which can expose data, credentials and software. Make the AMIs private or share only with specific accounts/organizations.

ec2ImageBlockPublicAccessOff.^description: AMI Block Public Access disabled: block public access for AMIs is 'unblocked' in {$COUNT} region(s). Enable it (block-new-sharing) to prevent AMIs from being made public. Existing public AMIs are reported separately.

ec2ImdsDefaultNotRequired.^description: IMDSv2 not required by default: in {$COUNT} region(s) the account-level instance metadata defaults do not set HttpTokens=required (or set a hop limit above 2), so new instances can be launched with IMDSv1. Set the account default to require IMDSv2 so new launches are protected; existing instances are covered by EC2IMDSv2.
ec2ImdsDefaultNotRequired.shortDesc: Require IMDSv2 by default for new instances
ref: [Set IMDSv2 as the default for the account]<https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/configuring-IMDS-new-instances.html#set-imdsv2-account-defaults>

ec2SnapshotBlockPublicAccessOff.^description: EBS snapshot Block Public Access disabled: block public access for EBS snapshots is 'unblocked' in {$COUNT} region(s), so snapshots can be shared publicly. Enable block-all-sharing (or at least block-new-sharing). Existing public snapshots are reported by EBSSnapshotIsPublic.
ec2SnapshotBlockPublicAccessOff.shortDesc: Enable EBS snapshot Block Public Access

elbAccessLogsDisabled.^description: Load balancer access logs disabled: {$COUNT} load balancer(s) do not deliver access logs to Amazon S3. Access logs are needed to investigate security events and troubleshoot traffic.

elbTlsPolicyOutdated.^description: Outdated TLS policy: {$COUNT} load balancer(s) have HTTPS/TLS/SSL listeners whose security policy still allows TLS 1.0, TLS 1.1 or SSLv3. Use a policy that supports only TLS 1.2 and later (e.g. ELBSecurityPolicy-TLS13-1-2-2021-06).
elbTlsPolicyOutdated.shortDesc: Load balancer TLS policy allows TLS 1.0/1.1

elbUsesIamOrImportedCert.^description: Load balancer uses IAM server certificates: {$COUNT} load balancer(s) have HTTPS/TLS/SSL listeners serving a certificate stored in IAM (server-certificate). IAM server certificates are not renewed automatically, are only manageable through the API/CLI and expire silently unless tracked elsewhere. Use certificates issued by AWS Certificate Manager (ACM), which renew automatically. Imported ACM certificates (also not auto-renewed) are reported separately by the ACM check acmImportedCertNoAutoRenewal.
elbUsesIamOrImportedCert.shortDesc: Load balancer listener uses an IAM server certificate
elbUsesIamOrImportedCert.remediation: aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn <listener-arn> --certificates CertificateArn=<acm-certificate-arn> (Classic: aws elb set-load-balancer-listener-ssl-certificate --load-balancer-name <name> --load-balancer-port 443 --ssl-certificate-id <acm-certificate-arn>)

ebsRecycleBinMissing.^description: Recycle Bin not protecting backups: in {$COUNT} region(s) there is no Recycle Bin retention rule for EBS snapshots and/or AMIs, so deleted snapshots/AMIs cannot be recovered. Create region-level retention rules (without exclusion tags, which leave the excluded resources unprotected) and lock them so they cannot be removed by a compromised principal.
ebsRecycleBinMissing.shortDesc: Create locked Recycle Bin rules for snapshots/AMIs

ebsSnapshotSharedExternally.^description: EBS snapshot shared outside the organization: {$COUNT} self-owned EBS snapshot(s) grant createVolumePermission to AWS accounts outside your AWS Organization (or the account is not in an organization). Those accounts can copy the data. Remove sharing that is not required.

ebsSnapshotUnencrypted.^description: Unencrypted EBS snapshot: {$COUNT} self-owned EBS snapshot(s), including AMI backing snapshots, are not encrypted. Volumes and AMIs created from them are unencrypted, and anyone the snapshot is shared or copied to can read the data without KMS key access. Copy the snapshot with encryption enabled, update AMIs to use the encrypted copy and delete the unencrypted snapshot.

ec2AllowedAmisNotEnforced.^description: Allowed AMIs not enforced: Allowed AMIs is disabled or only in audit mode in {$COUNT} region(s). Without it any AMI, including unvetted public AMIs, can be discovered and launched. Define image criteria for your trusted AMI providers, validate them in audit mode, then enable the setting (or manage it with an EC2 declarative policy).
ec2AllowedAmisNotEnforced.shortDesc: Allowed AMIs disabled or audit-mode only
ref: [Control the discovery and use of AMIs with Allowed AMIs]<https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-allowed-amis.html>
ec2AllowedAmisNotEnforced.remediation: aws ec2 replace-image-criteria-in-allowed-images-settings --image-criteria 'ImageProviders=[amazon,<account-id>]' && aws ec2 enable-allowed-images-settings --allowed-images-settings-state enabled

ec2AmiSharedExternally.^description: AMI shared outside the organization: {$COUNT} self-owned AMI(s) grant launch permission to AWS accounts or organizations outside your AWS Organization (or the account is not in an organization). Those accounts can launch the AMI and copy its snapshots. Remove sharing that is not required, or share with your organization or OUs instead.

ec2AmiUntrustedOrStale.^description: Instances on stale or untrusted AMIs: {$COUNT} running instance(s) were launched from an AMI that is deregistered (or no longer shared), deprecated or disabled, or from a public AMI whose owner is not Amazon, AWS Marketplace or a verified provider. Their software provenance and patch baseline cannot be confirmed. Rebuild them from a current, trusted (ideally your own golden) AMI.
ec2AmiUntrustedOrStale.shortDesc: Instance AMI stale or from unverified owner

ec2InstanceInPublicSubnet.^description: Workloads in public subnets: {$COUNT} EC2 instance(s) or RDS / ElastiCache / ECS network interface(s) are in subnets whose route table sends 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 to an internet gateway. Internal tiers placed there are one public IP or security-group change away from internet exposure. Move internal tiers to private subnets and reach the internet through NAT gateways or VPC endpoints; keep only internet-facing load balancers and gateways in public subnets.
ec2InstanceInPublicSubnet.shortDesc: Internal resource in a public subnet

ec2InstanceWithKeyPair.^description: SSH key pair on SSM-managed instances: {$COUNT} running instance(s) reachable through Session Manager were launched with an SSH key pair. Long-lived SSH keys are hard to rotate and audit; Session Manager provides IAM-controlled, logged access without inbound ports. Remove the key from authorized_keys, close port 22 and launch new instances without a key pair. (KeyName shows only the launch-time key.)
ec2InstanceWithKeyPair.shortDesc: SSH key pair on Session Manager instance

ec2UserDataSecrets.^description: Credentials in user data: {$COUNT} EC2 instance(s) or launch template(s) have user data containing AWS access keys, secret keys, private keys or literal passwords. User data is readable by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstanceAttribute or ec2:DescribeLaunchTemplateVersions and by any process on the instance through IMDS. Rotate the exposed credentials, then fetch secrets at boot from Secrets Manager or Parameter Store using the instance role. Matched values are masked in this report.
ref: [Run commands when you launch an EC2 instance with user data input]<https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/user-data.html>

vpcEndpointPolicyFullAccess.^description: VPC endpoint with full-access policy: {$COUNT} VPC endpoint(s) use the default full-access endpoint policy (Principal, Action and Resource '*') without an organization or account condition. Any credentials, including those from other accounts, can reach any resource of the service through the endpoint. Restrict the policy with aws:PrincipalOrgID / aws:ResourceOrgID conditions as part of a data perimeter.
vpcEndpointPolicyFullAccess.shortDesc: VPC endpoint uses default full-access policy
ref: [Control access to VPC endpoints using endpoint policies]<https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-access.html>

vpcNoGatewayEndpoints.^description: VPC private subnets without an S3 endpoint: {$COUNT} VPC(s) have private subnets (no default route to an internet gateway) whose route table is not associated with an S3 gateway endpoint, and the VPC has no S3 interface endpoint. S3 traffic from those subnets leaves the VPC through a NAT device and the public S3 endpoint (or cannot reach S3 at all), and cannot be restricted with an endpoint policy. Add a free S3 gateway endpoint (and a DynamoDB one if the VPC uses DynamoDB) and associate it with the private route tables.
vpcNoGatewayEndpoints.shortDesc: Private subnets lack an S3 gateway endpoint

vpcPeeringFullRoute.^description: Peering routes open whole VPCs of other accounts: {$COUNT} VPC(s) have a route to an active VPC peering connection whose destination equals or contains an entire CIDR block of a peer VPC owned by another AWS account, so every subnet of that external network is reachable from the associated subnets (and vice versa where the peer routes back). Where only some peer subnets need to be reached (for example a partner's API tier), route just those subnet CIDRs and keep security groups and network ACLs as the second layer of control. Same-account peering and transit gateway routes covering a whole peer CIDR are the documented default and are reported as review items (informational) only; default and summary routes to a transit gateway (hub-and-spoke egress / inspection) are not evaluated as full peer routes.
vpcPeeringFullRoute.shortDesc: Cross-account peering route covers whole peer VPC
ref: [Update your route tables for a VPC peering connection]<https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/peering/vpc-peering-routing.html>
vpcPeeringFullRoute.remediation: aws ec2 delete-route --route-table-id <route-table-id> --destination-cidr-block <peer-vpc-cidr> && aws ec2 create-route --route-table-id <route-table-id> --destination-cidr-block <required-peer-subnet-cidr> --vpc-peering-connection-id <pcx-id> (or --transit-gateway-id <tgw-id>)

vpnWeakTunnelCrypto.^description: Site-to-Site VPN tunnels allow weak cryptography: {$COUNT} VPN connection(s) have tunnels that still accept IKEv1, SHA1 integrity or weak Diffie-Hellman groups (2, 5, or only group 14). Empty tunnel option lists mean the AWS defaults, which include these legacy options for compatibility. Restrict each tunnel to IKEv2, SHA2-256 or stronger and DH groups 19-21 (coordinate with the customer gateway configuration first).
vpnWeakTunnelCrypto.shortDesc: VPN tunnels permit IKEv1/SHA1/weak DH groups

albMtlsOff.^description: ALB mutual TLS accepts expired client certificates: {$COUNT} Application Load Balancer(s) have HTTPS listeners with mutual TLS in verify mode but IgnoreClientCertificateExpiry enabled, so clients presenting expired (and possibly no longer controlled) certificates are still authenticated. Disable IgnoreClientCertificateExpiry and keep a revocation list on the trust store. Listeners without mTLS (off) and passthrough mode are reported as informational only, because whether mTLS is needed depends on the clients (for service-to-service traffic consider mTLS in verify mode with a trust store).
albMtlsOff.shortDesc: ALB mTLS accepts expired client certificates
ref: [Mutual authentication with TLS in Application Load Balancer]<https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/mutual-authentication.html>

albTargetGroupPlaintext.^description: ALB sends plaintext HTTP outside the VPC: {$COUNT} Application Load Balancer(s) forward to HTTP target groups of type ip with registered targets outside the load balancer's VPC (peered VPC or on-premises over VPN / Direct Connect), so unencrypted traffic leaves the VPC. Use HTTPS target groups for these targets. HTTP target groups whose targets are inside the VPC (TLS terminated at the ALB) are the standard pattern and are reported as informational only; use HTTPS there where data classification or compliance requires end-to-end encryption in transit.
albTargetGroupPlaintext.shortDesc: ALB HTTP target group has targets outside VPC
ref: [Register targets with your target group (IP targets outside the VPC)]<https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/target-group-register-targets.html>

ec2AutoRecoveryDisabled.^description: EC2 automatic recovery disabled: {$COUNT} instance(s) have simplified automatic recovery explicitly disabled (MaintenanceOptions.AutoRecovery=disabled). After a system status check failure (underlying hardware issue) they are not moved to healthy hardware automatically.

ec2SshdRunning.^description: Remote login service running on SSM-managed instances: {$COUNT} Windows instance(s) reachable through Session Manager still run the RDP (TermService) or OpenSSH (sshd) service according to SSM Inventory (AWS:Service). Prefer Session Manager / Fleet Manager for interactive access and stop or disable the remote login service to reduce attack surface. SSM collects service inventory for Windows only, so Linux instances are not evaluated.
ec2SshdRunning.shortDesc: RDP/SSH service running on managed instance

imagebuilderNoPipeline.^description: No image build pipeline: in {$COUNT} Region(s) there is no enabled EC2 Image Builder pipeline and EC2 instances run stock Amazon-published AMIs directly, so hardening, patch baselines and security tooling are applied (if at all) at boot instead of being baked into a tested, versioned image. Build hardened golden images with EC2 Image Builder (for example with the CIS / STIG hardening components) or another pipeline (Packer, a central image factory account) and launch instances from them. Instances on self-owned, cross-account or AWS Marketplace (vendor appliance) AMIs are not flagged.
imagebuilderNoPipeline.shortDesc: No hardened image pipeline; instances use stock AMIs

naclAllowAllIngress.^description: Custom Network ACL allows all inbound traffic: {$COUNT} custom (non-default) Network ACL(s) associated with subnets allow all protocols and ports from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 with no lower-numbered deny rule, so they add no subnet-level filtering. An allow-all rule reached behind only narrow deny rules (one host, port or protocol) is reported as INFO for review. Restrict the inbound rules to the ports and source ranges the subnet tier needs (e.g. only from the load balancer subnets for an application tier) to add a second layer of defence behind security groups. Default NACLs, which allow all traffic by design, are not flagged.
naclAllowAllIngress.shortDesc: Custom NACL allows all inbound traffic
ref: [Control subnet traffic with network access control lists]<https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-network-acls.html>
[SEC05-BP02 Control traffic flow within your network layers]<https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/sec_network_protection_layered.html>

selfManagedDataStoreOnEc2.^description: Self-managed data store on EC2: {$COUNT} EC2 instance(s) appear to run a self-managed database, cache or search engine (a server package such as mysql-server, postgresql-server, redis or Microsoft SQL Server in SSM Inventory, or an attached security group that explicitly opens a default data-store port such as 3306, 5432, 1433, 1521, 27017, 6379, 11211, 9042 or 9200). You then own patching, encryption, backup and access control of the engine. Consider a managed service (Amazon RDS / Aurora, ElastiCache, DocumentDB, OpenSearch Service, Keyspaces) to shift that responsibility to AWS. This is a heuristic - port-only evidence on instances without SSM Inventory may be a proxy or a shared security group.
ref: [SEC01-BP04 Stay up to date with security threats and recommendations]<https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/security-pillar/sec_securely_operate_updated_threats.html>

sgIngressBroadCidr.^description: Security group ingress from very broad public CIDRs: {$COUNT} security group(s) allow inbound traffic from public IPv4 ranges larger than /16 (or IPv6 ranges larger than /32) other than 0.0.0.0/0 / ::/0, for example 0.0.0.0/1, 52.0.0.0/8 or 2000::/3. Such ranges cover large parts of the internet and bypass checks that only look for 0.0.0.0/0. Restrict the source to the specific addresses, prefix lists or security groups that need access. Broad private ranges (RFC 1918, CGNAT, ULA) are not flagged.
sgIngressBroadCidr.shortDesc: SG ingress from very broad public CIDR

sgUnrestrictedEgress.^description: Data-tier security group with unrestricted egress: {$COUNT} security group(s) attached to managed data stores (RDS / Aurora / Neptune / DocumentDB, ElastiCache, Redshift or OpenSearch network interfaces) allow all outbound traffic (or all TCP/UDP ports) to 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0. Data stores rarely need to initiate connections; open egress makes data exfiltration and command-and-control easier if the engine is compromised. Remove the default allow-all outbound rule and allow only the destinations the engine needs (e.g. a VPC endpoint or prefix list for S3 integration).
sgUnrestrictedEgress.shortDesc: Data-tier SG allows all outbound traffic

ssmVpcEndpointsMissing.^description: Isolated subnets without Systems Manager endpoints: {$COUNT} VPC(s) have EC2 instances in subnets with no default route (no internet gateway, NAT, transit gateway or other 0.0.0.0/0 / ::/0 path) and no ssm / ssmmessages interface VPC endpoint, so the SSM Agent cannot reach Systems Manager. These instances cannot be patched, inventoried or accessed through Session Manager, which pushes operators back to SSH keys and bastions. Create interface endpoints for com.amazonaws.<region>.ssm and ssmmessages (and ec2messages for SSM Agent < 3.3.40.0) with private DNS enabled. Instances whose SSM Agent is Online without in-VPC endpoints (e.g. through centralized endpoints in a shared-services VPC) are not flagged; partially Online fleets are reported as INFO.
ssmVpcEndpointsMissing.shortDesc: Isolated subnets lack SSM interface endpoints
